- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast 3–5 days after spike at 10–15% below true peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) in recent days, model underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast mean, especially if history shows mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); adjust downward by 1–3% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is flat (0.0) and history shows volatility, model tends to lag; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 5 days.
